Yangtze Basin & Central
Inland megacities and riverine industrial corridors. - Cities: Chengdu, Wuhan, Luzhou, Yichang, Nanchang, Zhangjiajie Explore Region →



Yangtze Delta & East
Interconnected manufacturing clusters and canal towns. - Cities: Taizhou, Yangzhou, Wuhu, Huangshan, Lianyungang Explore Region →






Yellow River & North Plain
Heavy industrial centers across the agricultural heartland. - Cities: Jinan, Zhengzhou, Baoding, Shijiazhuang, Zibo… Explore Region →



Northeast Rust Belt
Early industrial powerhouses and international border gateways. - Cities: Harbin, Dandong, Fuxin, Panjin, Tieling, Hunchun… Explore Region →

title: Data & Methodology
text: How this ratlas ingests, processes, and cartographically renders 30 years of satellite-detected urban expansion across China.

title: Data & Methodology
section: 1. Primary Data Source: DLR WSF Evolution
text:
1. Primary Data Source: DLR WSF Evolution
The physical urban growth data in this project is driven by the World Settlement Footprint Evolution (WSF Evolution) dataset, produced by the German Aerospace Center (DLR):

Spatial Resolution: 30 meters per pixel, derived from joint multi-decadal analysis of Landsat-5, Landsat-7, and Landsat-8 optical imagery, integrated with radar and digital elevation datasets.
Temporal Coverage: 1985 to 2015 (30-year span).
Pixel Semantics: Each pixel value encodes the exact calendar year (\(1985 \le  ext{year} \le 2015\)) in which human settlement was first detected. Value 0 represents non-urban surfaces (natural vegetation, bare land, agriculture, or water). Value 1985 represents human settlements already established by or prior to 1985.
Open Web Retrieval: Retrieved directly from DLR’s open data servers (download.geoservice.dlr.de) using GDAL virtual file streaming (/vsicurl/) and R’s terra package.

title: Data & Methodology
text:
2. Administrative Geodatabase & Extents

GADM 4.1 (Database of Global Administrative Areas): Provided level 0 (national outline), level 1 (provincial boundaries), and level 2 (prefectural boundaries).
Centroids & Analysis Radii: Urban core extents were established for each city based on high-density metropolitan boundaries, ranging from 12 km to 30 km radius depending on city tier and metropolitan scale.
Coordinate Reference Systems: Base data in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), with surface area calculations performed using ellipsoidal pixel geometry (terra::cellSize(unit = "km")) to eliminate high-latitude area distortion.

title: Data & Methodology
text:
3. Four Landmark Urban Development Epochs
Urban expansion in modern China has unfolded in distinct historical waves:

Pre-1985 Core (#F59E0B · Amber Gold): The pre-reform base urban footprint. This includes ancient historical city cores and the industrial settlements constructed during the early Five-Year Plans (1949–1980).
1986–1995 Wave (#EF4444 · Crimson Coral): Deng Xiaoping’s 1992 Southern Tour (Nanxun), the launch of Special Economic Zones (SEZs), and the initial surge of rural-to-urban industrialization.
1996–2005 Wave (#06B6D4 · Electric Cyan): China’s 2001 accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO), the emergence of the “Factory of the World”, highway grid expansion, and initial high-tech development zones.
2006–2015 Wave (#10B981 · Emerald Green): The High-Speed Rail (HSR) construction boom, the Western Development Strategy (Xibu Da Kaifa), massive State-level New Areas (Guojiaji Xinqu), and metropolitan amalgamation.

title: Data & Methodology
text:
4. Quantitative Metrics
For each city, the following metrics are computed:

Cumulative Built-Up Area (\(A_t\)): Total surface area in $ ext{km}^2$ occupied by detected settlements at year \(t\).
Net Spatial Gain (\(\Delta A\)): \(A_{2015} - A_{1985}\).
30-Year Growth Multiple (\(M\)): \(A_{2015} / A_{1985}\).
Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR): \(\left( rac{A_{2015}}{A_{1985}}
ight)^{1/30} - 1\).

title: Data & Methodology
text:
5. Cartographic Stack & Tools

Language & Runtime: R (v4.6.1) & Python 3
Spatial Processing: terra (v1.9), sf (v1.0), tidyterra
Visualization: ggplot2, patchwork, ragg
Typography: CJK rendering via system font Droid Sans Fallback with bilingual typesetting
